title: Julia Roberts Pays Tribute to “Steel Magnolias” Co‑Star Tom Skerritt After His Death at 93
body:
Julia Roberts paid tribute on Thursday to Tom Skerritt, the 93‑year‑old actor who portrayed her father in the beloved 1989 film *Steel Magnolias*, after news of his passing spread across social media and industry circles. The Oscar‑nominated star shared a heartfelt message on Instagram, recalling the warmth and mentorship Skerritt offered during the production and expressing gratitude for the indelible mark he left on her early career. Skerritt’s death marks the end of a six‑decade‑long journey that saw him evolve from a rugged television leading man to a venerable character actor whose work spanned generations.

Skerritt, whose career began in the late 1950s with guest spots on shows such as *The Twilight Zone* and *Gunsmoke*, became a fixture of American cinema in the 1970s with roles in *M*A*S*H* (1970) and *The Last Picture Show* (1971). Yet it was his turn as Drum Eatenton, the gentle, supportive father to Roberts’ character Annelle, that cemented his place in popular culture. *Steel Magnolias*—a Southern‑flavored ensemble drama that also featured Sally Field, Dolly Parton and Daryl Hannah—remains a touchstone for its blend of humor, heartbreak, and strong female friendships. Skerritt’s understated performance provided the film’s emotional anchor, and his chemistry with the young Roberts was noted by critics as a highlight that helped launch her ascent to stardom.

Roberts’ tribute highlighted not only the personal bond they shared on set but also the broader influence Skerritt wielded on younger actors. In her caption, she wrote, “You taught me how to be kind, generous, and to always give my best, no matter the role.” Industry insiders echo this sentiment, recalling stories of Skerritt’s willingness to mentor emerging talent, whether by offering advice on delivering a line or simply sharing a quiet moment backstage. His reputation as a consummate professional—known for arriving early, respecting crew members, and maintaining a collaborative atmosphere—made him a beloved figure on set and a model for the work ethic many actors strive to emulate.

The passing of Skerritt arrives at a moment when Hollywood is reflecting on the contributions of its senior generation. In recent months, the industry has mourned the losses of other iconic performers such as Sidney Poitier, Michael Gambon and Angela Lansbury, prompting conversations about preserving cinematic heritage. Film historians point out that Skerritt’s body of work, which includes notable collaborations with directors like Robert Altman (*M*A*S*H*) and Martin Scorsese (*The Last Temptation of Christ*), offers a living archive of evolving storytelling styles from the New Hollywood era to contemporary cinema. His ability to navigate both television and film, and to transition seamlessly between leading and supporting roles, exemplifies the adaptability that defined successful actors of his time.

Beyond his on‑screen legacy, Skerritt was an outspoken advocate for veterans’ issues and environmental causes, leveraging his public platform to raise awareness and funds. He served on the board of the United Service Organizations and participated in numerous charity events, underscoring a commitment to service that extended far beyond the silver screen. Such off‑camera contributions have inspired many in the entertainment community to engage more actively in philanthropy, reinforcing the idea that celebrity influence can be harnessed for societal good.

As the film community bids farewell to Tom Skerritt, his influence persists through the countless performers he mentored and the timeless films that continue to resonate with audiences. Julia Roberts’ tribute serves as a reminder that the bonds forged on set often transcend the fleeting nature of fame, leaving a lasting imprint on both personal lives and the broader cultural landscape. Looking ahead, industry leaders are calling for renewed efforts to document and celebrate the careers of veteran actors, ensuring that future generations can learn from the dedication, humility, and artistry embodied by figures like Skerritt. His legacy, anchored in both his memorable performances and his generosity off‑camera, will undoubtedly endure as a guiding light for aspiring artists worldwide.
